objectives: Hear /g/ followed immediately by /r/ at the beginning of a taught word.
Blend /g/ and /r/ smoothly without inserting a vowel between them.
Distinguish the initial gr blend from /g/ alone and other taught blends.
Say the complete word after blending the onset with the remaining sounds.
concepts: The initial gr blend contains /g/ followed by /r/.
Both consonant sounds remain audible in the blend.
No extra vowel belongs between /g/ and /r/.
Listening for the complete word confirms accurate blending.

definitions.definition: Two consonant sounds heard together at the beginning of a word.
A speech sound that can distinguish one word from another.
Joining speech sounds in order to say a word.

workedExamples.solution: Grab starts with /g/ followed by /r/; gap starts with /g/ alone.
Keep /g/ and /r/ together, then blend the rest of the word.

commonMistakes: Adding a vowel and saying guh-rab instead of blending smoothly.

Guessing before hearing the whole word.
keyTakeaways: Do not insert a vowel between the consonants.
